THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Weston's Community Development Authority voted unanimously to retire bond debt years early after closing a TIF district that added $354 million in assessed value, while Kronenwetter's Village Board pushed forward on several land-use and parks decisions.

  • The Village of Weston CDA voted unanimously to redeem its 2017A lease revenue bonds in full, wiping out debt payments that had been scheduled through 2031.
  • Weston's CDA will bring the question of its own potential disbandment to the Village Board after TIF District No. 1 — a 28-year run generating $95.7 million in increment — officially closed.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board approved rezoning Marathon County Highway Department property to M2 General Industrial, clearing the way for the county to proceed with facility development.
  • Kronenwetter's board approved a Bushka Park 5K/3K run/walk fundraiser for September 12, 2026, and directed staff to finalize details including matching a $5,000 parks grant.
  • Kronenwetter's board reached consensus to move forward on a zero-lot line ordinance change, directing staff and the Plan Commission to draft amendments modeled on neighboring communities.
  • Kronenwetter's CLIPP Committee is set to vote on a temporary moratorium on data center development applications and take up a proposed oak wilt ordinance at its Monday meeting.

Coming up: The Wausau School Board holds a special meeting and board workshop Monday, Aug. 4, to take up teacher salaries, employee handbook updates, and school perceptions survey results that could inform future referendum discussions. Marathon County's Health & Human Services Committee meets Thursday, Aug. 6, at 5:00 PM, and the Wausau School Board convenes its regular monthly meeting Monday, Aug. 10.
